_note: Measured on the DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, 128GB unified memory), ComfyUI 0.30.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130. Timing is taken from ComfyUI's own history timestamps, not from the proxy poll loop, so client latency cannot distort it. Every row had a warmup render first (excluded) to keep the ~22GB weight load out of the number, and the measured render used a different seed from the warmup so ComfyUI's execution cache cannot serve it.

graph.prompt: a paper boat drifting on a calm lake at sunset, gentle ripples, cinematic

results.reason: InductorError CppCompileError: fatal error Python.h -- python3-dev is not installed on this host and no passwordless sudo is available; ComfyUI's TorchCompileModel forces config.cpp_wrapper back to True at runtime, so TORCHINDUCTOR_CPP_WRAPPER=0 does not take effect. Not a speedup: the failed render returned in ~1s.

attention_ab._note: ComfyUI bakes its attention backend in at startup, so each side is a separate process. Same graph, same prompt, same seed on both sides.
attention_ab.microbenchmark_note: A standalone sageattn-vs-SDPA kernel sweep showed no consistent win at the shapes H3 actually uses: 4k tokens 0.95x, 8k tokens 1.03x, 16k tokens 1.12x, head_dim 128 1.02x, bf16 0.98x. The end-to-end 1.058x is therefore not attributable to attention alone; H3 spends enough of its time in attention for the small wins at 8k+ tokens to matter.

noise_floor._note: THE MOST IMPORTANT NUMBER IN THIS FILE. Identical configuration, run twice back to back on an idle machine, gave 274.4s and 328.9s -- a 19.9% spread. The same configuration also produced 448.8s in another session. So any single-run speedup smaller than roughly 20% on this host cannot be distinguished from noise.
noise_floor.root_cause: ds4-server (DeepSeek V4, --ctx 32768) holds 103 GB of the 130.6 GB unified memory. ComfyUI's free VRAM therefore floats between ~11.4 GB and ~100 GB while H3 weights are ~22 GB, so the model is fully resident when memory is free and gets split/paged when it is not. ComfyUI's own log shows per-step denoising cost for one identical configuration ranging from 1.78 s/it to 92.11 s/it.
noise_floor.evidence: GET /system_stats during contention reported vram_free = 11433387040 (10.6 GiB) out of vram_total = 130663591936 (121.7 GiB); nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps showed ds4-server using 103446 MiB.
noise_floor.consequence: The 1.113x (fp8) and 1.058x (sage) single-point results sit inside this band and must be read as 'not slower', not 'faster'. Only the best-sample fp8+sage figure (~1.20x vs baseline) exceeds the band.

launch_flag_ab._note: The systemd unit comfyui-dgx.service is enabled via default.target.wants, so it runs at every boot and its ExecStart flags are the ones that actually persist. These rows compare that unit's flags against the flags used for the headline measurement.
launch_flag_ab.conclusion: --lowvram costs ~1.05x on the PyTorch side and the same ordering holds with sage. Direction is unambiguous (forced weight splitting only adds CPU<->GPU page traffic and cannot remove work), so removing it is safe even though the magnitude sits near the noise band.

sageattention_on_dgx_spark.report: A user reported semi-corrupted output when running a Wan 2.2 video workflow on DGX Spark with sage attention. No official resolution is recorded.
sageattention_on_dgx_spark.mitigation: Installed wheel is unmodified upstream v2.2.0 built with TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.0, not the Sage 3 Blackwell path that #297 describes (which additionally requires hand-editing api.cu). Every H3 render was verified frame-by-frame visually plus an audio RMS check, not just 'status: succeeded'.
sageattention_on_dgx_spark.revert: Remove --use-sage-attention from scripts/comfyui-dgx.service. Costs ~1.05x, itself near the noise floor.

tensorrt_support_correction.originally_claimed: GB10 sm_121 has no public record of TensorRT support
tensorrt_support_correction.corrected: The official TensorRT Edge-LLM support matrix lists NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10) as an Official target (CUDA 13.0 + TensorRT 10, system package). See https://nvidia.github.io/TensorRT-Edge-LLM/latest/user_guide/getting_started/support-matrix.html
tensorrt_support_correction.reason_still_not_adopted: Not installed locally; ComfyUI's H3 path uses no TensorRT node so adoption means writing an engine and replacing the DiT node; and SM12x has only 99 KiB shared memory vs 227 KiB on SM100, which overflows CUTLASS's SM120 tile configs (https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/12141).
